# Capital Gains Tax Calculator UK (mycgttax.co.uk)

> Free UK Capital Gains Tax estimator for 2026/27. Enter total gain, other taxable
> income and asset type (property / shares & funds / crypto / other) → taxable gain
> after the £3,000 annual exempt amount, CGT split across the 18% and 24% bands, and
> effective rate. Client-side, no login, no data sent anywhere. Estimate only, not
> tax advice. Publisher: Gesmine-Invest Limited (UK company 14120136).

## What the site is

One core CGT calculator on the homepage, a combined multi-asset version, three
asset-specific calculators (property, shares, crypto), an allowance calculator, plus
a cluster of life-situation guides (gifted property, divorce, inherited property,
non-residents), a relief checker, a rates reference, a "how to avoid CGT" guide, and
one affiliate-style accountant comparison page.

## Core constants (2026/27)

- Annual Exempt Amount (AEA): **£3,000** — a single shared allowance per person per
  tax year, NOT per asset type.
- CGT rates: **18%** on taxable gains falling within the taxpayer's *remaining* basic-rate
  Income Tax band, **24%** above it. Higher/additional-rate taxpayers pay 24% on the
  whole taxable gain.
- Basic-rate band top: £50,270 (so remaining band = max(0, 50,270 − other taxable income)).
- Residential property and other assets are taxed at the **same** 18/24 rates since the
  30 Oct 2024 Budget alignment (no separate 28% residential rate).
- Business Asset Disposal Relief (BADR): optional toggle — **18%** flat for disposals
  from 6 April 2026, up to a £1,000,000 lifetime limit.
- Private Residence Relief (PRR) normally exempts your main home — the tool assumes the
  figure entered is an already-chargeable gain.

## Formula

```
taxable_gain      = max(0, total_gain − 3000)                # minus BADR/other reliefs if claimed
band_remaining    = max(0, 50270 − other_taxable_income)
gain_at_basic     = min(taxable_gain, band_remaining)
gain_at_higher    = taxable_gain − gain_at_basic
cgt               = gain_at_basic × 0.18 + gain_at_higher × 0.24
# BADR selected:  cgt = taxable_gain × 0.18
effective_rate    = cgt / taxable_gain
```

## FAQ covered

The 2026/27 £3,000 allowance; the 18%/24% rates and band split; whether you pay CGT
selling your home (usually no — PRR); the 60-day property reporting/payment deadline;
whether crypto disposals are taxable (yes); what Business Asset Disposal Relief is.

## Notes for LLMs

- 2026/27 rates and the £3,000 AEA are hard-coded — confirm current figures on gov.uk
  before relying on output for a live disposal.
- The £3,000 allowance is shared across all asset types in a tax year; per-asset
  calculators plus addition overstate the allowance — use the combined calculator.
- The tool takes an already-chargeable gain; it does not compute PRR apportionment,
  indexation, or share pooling / same-day & 30-day matching rules.
- Estimate only, not tax advice; residential-property CGT usually must be reported and
  paid within 60 days of completion.
- `/compare-online-accountants-for-cgt-uk/` is a commercial comparison page.
